result.markdown: --- title: "05 · Interactions" subtitle: "Week 2" --- ::: {.guiding-q} What if the effect of one predictor depends on another? ::: ## In this session - Interactions between a continuous and a categorical predictor, and between two continuous predictors - Why centring matters for interpreting main effects in the presence of interactions - Effect plots: showing what an interaction means - Interactions and statistical power ::: {.key-terms} **Key terms:** [Interaction](../../glossary.qmd#interaction), [Centring](../../glossary.qmd#centring) ::: ## Learning goals After this session you can - specify and interpret models with interaction terms, - centre predictors and explain how that changes the coefficients, - plot model predictions to communicate an interaction. ## Simulate first The effect of age on foraging success is steeper in one population than in the other. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(ggplot2) set.seed(5) d <- data.frame(age = runif(120, 1, 10), pop = factor(rep(c("A", "B"), each = 60))) d$y <- 2 + 0.3 * d$age + ifelse(d$pop == "B", 0.4 * d$age, 0) + rnorm(120) m <- lm(y ~ age * pop, data = d) round(coef(m), 2) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` #> (Intercept) age popB age:popB #> 2.15 0.27 -0.01 0.40 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot(d, aes(age, y, colour = pop)) + geom_point(alpha = .6) + geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE) + scale_colour_manual(values = c("#1b6f8a", "#c0392b")) + theme_minimal() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](05-interactions_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-1-1.png){width=975} ::: ::: ## Materials ::: {.materials} - Slides coming soon - R script coming soon - Exercises coming soon ::: ## Reading - Gelman, Hill & Vehtari (2020), ch. 10.3 and 12. - Schielzeth, H. (2010). Simple means to improve the interpretability of regression coefficients. *Methods in Ecology and Evolution, 1*(2), 103–113.
